item.title: A Social History of "Operators" in Mathematics
item.description: A social history of the mathematical “operator”: how actions like differentiation became objects you can manipulate, classify, and build theories around—shaped by notation, education, disciplinary disputes, and the demands of physics and engineering.

item.title: The Semantics of "Geometry" from Euler to Today (Europe & the United States)
item.description: A historical-semantic survey of what “geometry” has meant in mathematics from Euler’s 18th-century contrast with analysis through modern differential, topological, algebraic, and computational geometries, focusing on Europe and the United States.
